When you work with APIs, you are essentially asking another program for data or services. This is done through HTTP requests, which are like messages you send to a server. Most APIs now return data in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and computers to read. However, you often need to prove who you are before getting access. This usually involves authentication, such as using an API key or a token.

Be aware that many APIs have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests in a given period. If you exceed this, you might get blocked temporarily. Therefore, it’s crucial to build good error handling into your code. Always check if a request was successful, and if not, read the error message. This will save you a lot of time and frustration.
